I upgraded 8 production dependencies and refreshed 4 others in the lockfile, which removes the vulnerabilities this app can actually hit. The server boots, and every backend test passes except the 19 MQTT tests, which fail because the MQTT test container (HiveMQ) won't start on this machine.

**What changed** (only `package.json` and `package-lock.json`)

| Package | Old → New | How it's reachable here |
|---|---|---|
| jsonata | 2.1.1 → 2.2.2 | Critical: user-written JSON queries (HTTP, MQTT, MongoDB monitors) could run arbitrary code on the server |
| protobufjs | 7.2.6 → 7.6.6 | Critical: the gRPC monitor parses user-supplied `.proto` definitions (code injection, DoS) |
| @grpc/grpc-js | 1.8.22 → 1.14.6 | A gRPC server being monitored could crash the app with a malformed compressed message |
| axios | 0.32.0 → 0.34.0 | Used by every HTTP monitor and most notification senders (prototype-pollution and proxy issues) |
| follow-redirects (lockfile only) | 1.16.0 → 1.16.2 | Used by axios; login headers could leak across redirects |
| mysql2 | 3.11.5 → 3.24.6 | A monitored MySQL server could force a downgrade that leaks the password in plain text, or exhaust memory |
| nodemailer | 7.0.13 → 10.2.1 | The SMTP monitor connects to the servers it watches; a hostile one could stall the process with crafted replies |
| liquidjs | 10.26.0 → 10.29.0 | Notification templates (infinite loop and memory-limit bypasses) |
| ws | 8.19.0 → 8.21.3 | The WebSocket monitor (memory-exhaustion DoS); also removes three duplicate copies |
| body-parser, proxy-addr, engine.io (lockfile only) | small updates | Request-body DoS, IP spoofing when "trust proxy" is on, socket.io DoS |

**Policy and compatibility**
- **Release age:** `.npmrc` sets `min-release-age=14`, but npm 10.8.2 ignores that setting. I enforced it with `--before` and checked all 16 changed lockfile entries; each is 15 days old or more. That ruled out some newer versions, e.g. ws 8.22.x and liquidjs 10.30.x.
- **Install scripts:** in `allowScripts` I swapped `protobufjs@7.2.6` for `protobufjs@7.6.6`, since the new version still has an install script.
- **nodemailer 7 → 10 is a major-version jump.** I checked its breaking changes: a renamed error code the app never uses, stricter certificate checks on remote attachments/OAuth2/proxies (the app uses none of these), and Node ≥20 (the app already requires ≥20.4). Nothing affects this app.

**Verification**
- Backend tests: 225 of 244 pass. The 19 failures are all MQTT tests. HiveMQ's Java process crashes on startup in this Docker setup, independent of my change; I didn't re-run the MQTT tests on the original tree.
- Since those MQTT tests also exercise jsonata, I ran the app's `evaluateJsonQuery` directly. Normal queries work, and a `constructor`-chain code-execution attempt fails with an error instead of running.
- A separate script exercised liquid rendering, proto parsing, the gRPC client, and sending mail through nodemailer. The server boots and serves pages; on an empty data folder it starts in database-setup mode.

**Left alone on purpose** (`npm audit` still lists these; none can be reached at runtime)
- **tar, node-gyp, cacache, make-fetch-happen, @louislam/sqlite3:** used only during install, or by the setup script that downloads a release from the project's own GitHub.
- **compression:** listed as a dependency but never imported.
- **qs:** every advisory needs options the app and Express don't use (`comma`, `plainObjects`/`allowPrototypes`). The fixed version Express would need is too new under the 14-day rule.
- **undici:** cheerio only calls `load()`, so undici's network code never runs, and http-cookie-agent is used only through its plain-HTTP entrypoint.
- **redbean-node → lodash/glob/minimatch:** `_.template` isn't used, and glob only scans fixed model folders.
- **@azure/msal-node:** the vulnerable login flow isn't used by the SQL Server driver.
- **ip-address:** only parses admin-configured proxy settings.
- **Dev tooling** (vite, vue-i18n, testcontainers, eslint plugins, etc.): not part of the running server.
